extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal education funding (school administrators and Title IX Coordinators), campus Title IX personnel, institutional counsel, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and requirements for how recipients must respond to formal complaints of sexual harassment under Title IX, including what procedures must be followed, the rights of parties, and the duties of Title IX Coordinators and other personnel. Covers obligations to offer supportive measures, when to file or dismiss complaints, documentation requirements, and limits on mandatory filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the entirety of §106.45 when a formal complaint is filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are expected to comply with the entirety of the §106.45 grievance process whenever a formal complaint is filed, regardless of whether the recipient believes failure to comply was “not clearly unreasonable.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department may find a violation for failure to follow any required provision of §106.45 (e.g., failing to provide required written notice), even if the recipient believes it had a good reason. The grievance process is the standardized framework to resolve formal complaints alleging Title IX sexual harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice of allegations (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide the requisite written notice of allegations to both parties as required by §106.45(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to send the initial written notice to both parties can be a violation of §106.45(b)(2) even if recipient believes it had a good reason not to send it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to present witnesses and evidence (§106.45(b)(5)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide an equal opportunity for the parties to present witnesses (fact and expert) and other inculpatory and exculpatory evidence as part of the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denying opportunities to present witnesses or evidence may violate §106.45(b)(5)(ii), regardless of the recipient's subjective belief about the reasonableness of that denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights for dismissal (§106.45(b)(8)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant whose allegations in a formal complaint are dismissed may appeal such a dismissal on specific grounds under §106.45(b)(8)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grievance process includes appeal procedures that protect complainant and respondent rights and contribute to predictability and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of §106.45 (applies only to Title IX sexual harassment as defined in §106.30 within U.S. programs/activities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The §106.45 grievance process applies only to formal complaints alleging sexual harassment as defined in §106.30 that occurred in the recipient's education program or activity against a person in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations do not prescribe the process recipients must use for other types of misconduct; recipients may address out-of-jurisdiction incidents through non-Title IX codes of conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality, no conflicts of interest, and objective examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the §106.45 grievance process is to resolve allegations impartially, without conflicts of interest or bias, and to objectively examine relevant evidence before reaching a determination regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX personnel must be free from conflicts of interest and bias (§106.45(b)(1)(iii)). The process is designed to foster fairness, reliability, predictability, and legitimacy of outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must not prejudge or summarily dismiss formal complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complainant files a formal complaint, the recipient should not prejudge or subject the complaint to cursory or conclusory evaluation instead of following the §106.45 grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting recipients to deem allegations meritless or frivolous without following §106.45 would defeat the Department's goals and could increase risk that victims are not provided remedies; however limited discretionary dismissal grounds remain available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of informal resolution and discretionary dismissal (§106.45(b)(9) & (b)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients retain discretion to offer informal resolution to resolve formal complaints (§106.45(b)(9)) and may permissibly dismiss a formal complaint (or allegations) under limited circumstances (§106.45(b)(3)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretionary dismissal circumstances include complainant withdrawal in writing, respondent no longer enrolled or employed, or specific circumstances preventing collection of sufficient evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint participation requirement (§106.30 revision)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of filing a formal complaint, the complainant must be participating in or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revision to the definition of “formal complaint” clarifies standing to file a formal complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary dismissal grounds (§106.45(b)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may dismiss a formal complaint where the complainant wishes to withdraw the formal complaint in writing, where the respondent is no longer enrolled or employed, or where specific circumstances prevent collecting sufficient evidence to reach a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The elapsed time between an incident and filing may justify discretionary dismissal if it prevents collecting sufficient evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: No statute of limitations imposed for filing a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to include a requirement limiting the amount of time a complainant has for filing a formal complaint (no statute of limitations in these final regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length of time may nonetheless affect ability to collect evidence and support discretionary dismissal in particular circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate to comply with §106.44(a) with or without a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with §106.44(a) — including offering supportive measures — whether or not a formal complaint is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.45(b)(1) adds this mandate; recipients are on notice they must offer supportive measures and treat complainants and respondents equitably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator discretion regarding filing formal complaints (removal of proposed §106.44(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators retain discretion to sign and file a formal complaint after receiving reports (including multiple reports) and are not required to file simply because multiple reports were received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department removed proposed mandatory filing for multiple reports to respect complainant autonomy and avoid chilling reporting; Title IX Coordinators may consider factors (e.g., pattern of alleged misconduct) in deciding whether signing is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator signing a formal complaint does not make them the complainant or party
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Title IX Coordinator signs a formal complaint, that action is not taken “on behalf of” the complainant and the Title IX Coordinator does not become a complainant or otherwise a party to the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Title IX Coordinator acts on behalf of the recipient to institute a grievance process and must remain impartial under §106.45(b)(1)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator must promptly contact complainant about supportive measures and consider complainant's wishes
rubrics_metrics.description: Before or in connection with signing a formal complaint, the Title IX Coordinator must promptly contact the complainant to discuss availability of supportive measures, consider the complainant's wishes, and explain the process for filing a formal complaint (per §106.44(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contact requirement is part of ensuring complainant autonomy and informed decision-making; the Coordinator's decision to sign should take into account the complainant's wishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination/hearing reliance rule (§106.45(b)(6)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party or witness does not submit to cross-examination at the hearing, the decision-maker must not rely on any statement of that party or witness in reaching a determination regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a practical constraint against filing complaints that will be futile when no complaining witness is willing to participate in cross-examination at a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: No coercion to participate; complainant not obligated to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complainant does not wish to participate in a grievance process (including being cross-examined at a live hearing), the recipient is not permitted to threaten, coerce, intimidate, or discriminate against the complainant to secure participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a Title IX Coordinator signs a formal complaint, the complainant need not appear at a live hearing or be cross-examined; recipients must respect the complainant's choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against retaliation and right not to participate (§106.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.71 prohibits retaliation and expressly protects any person's right not to participate in a Title IX proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must not retaliate against individuals for choosing not to participate and must ensure protections are communicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: No supportive-measures safe harbor; supportive measures are required and must be documented if not provided (§106.44(a) & §106.45(b)(10)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department removed the proposed safe harbor that would have shielded recipients for offering supportive measures in lieu of investigation; instead, recipients are required to offer supportive measures and must document why not providing supportive measures was not clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients cannot treat supportive measures as an optional safe harbor to avoid Title IX obligations; §106.45(b)(10)(ii) imposes documentation obligations and §106.45(b)(10) addresses recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal authority (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have authority under §106.44(c) to order emergency removal of a respondent where the situation arising from sexual harassment allegations presents a risk to the physical health or safety of any person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency removal may be used even in absence of a formal complaint to address imminent safety concerns; nothing prevents contacting law enforcement as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of reasons for response decisions (deliberate-indifference recordkeeping, §106.45(b)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.45(b)(10) requires recipients to document reasons for conclusions about their response to reported sexual harassment (including why the response was not deliberately indifferent and reasons related to supportive measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Department declined to require documentation of every decision not to initiate a formal complaint, it does require recipients to document why certain responses (or failures to act) were not clearly unreasonable given the circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to address allegations outside Title IX jurisdiction through other codes of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Where alleged harassment did not occur within the recipient's education program or activity, §106.45(b)(3) may require dismissal for Title IX purposes, but recipients may choose to address such allegations through non-Title IX codes of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarification reduces tension between jurisdictional dismissals and institutional responsibilities to address misconduct that affects their community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of survivor autonomy, campus safety, and efficient use of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions about signing formal complaints should balance complainant autonomy, campus safety, and efficient use of institutional resources; mandatory filing (as proposed then removed) was rejected in favor of Coordinator discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX Coordinators may consider factors such as patterns of alleged misconduct, threats, or violence, but are not compelled to file formal complaints in every multiple-report scenario.
